steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
To make the crust: Blend 2 cups flour, softened butter, and 1/2 cup sugar in a medium bowl until well combined.
Press crust into the bottom of an ungreased 9x13-inch pan.
Bake crust in the preheated oven until firm and golden, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, make the filling: Whisk remaining 1 1/2 cups sugar and 1/4 cup flour in a medium bowl. Whisk in eggs, then lemon juice until smooth.
Pour filling over the baked crust.
Bake in the preheated oven for 20 minutes. Set the pan aside to cool completely; the bars will firm up as they cool.
When cooled, cut bars into uniform squares.

raw_recipe.headline: The Best Lemon Bars
raw_recipe.description: These lemon bars are easy to make with fresh lemons and simple ingredients you probably already have for a deliciously rich and tart treat.

video.description: In this video, you'll learn how to make lemon bars with chef Nicole McLaughlin. The recipe is simple, featuring a sweet and crumbly cookie crust and a rich and flavorful lemon filling made with fresh lemon juice and eggs. She takes you through the entire process, from making the crust to preparing the filling and baking the bars to perfection. Whether you're a seasoned baker or a beginner, this recipe is sure to wow your friends and family.

review.reviewBody: Excellent, everything a true lemon bar should be. Buttery, tender and tart. Definitely use at least 1/2 cup of lemon juice or more. I've made this recipe many times and find that 2/3 cups lemon juice (juice of 3 large lemons) gives this the perfect tartness. (add 1 extra tablespoon flour if using 2/3 cup juice) I also added the zest of 2 of the lemons. I made this in an 8 X 11 dish (smaller than what the recipe calls for) and found it ideal. The crust is the perfect thickness and there is enough lemon custard in each bite to satisfy. This recipe makes a lot of crust and does spread into a 9 x 13 dish easily, but makes a thinner bar. If using the smaller baking dish (i.e, 8 X 11), make sure to increase cooking time of the crust and filling an extra 5-10 min each. As another reviewer stated, it's better to overcook then undercook the crust. Also, add 1/4 teaspoon salt to the crust for more flavor. This will be my master recipe for Lemon Bars.

As printed, this recipe was not lemony enough. Using other's suggestions, I tried it again using the juice of 5 lemons (a little over 2/3 cup) and the zest of two lemons. I also added 1/3 c. flour to compensate for the extra liquid. I also had to increase the bake time to about 24 minutes. These turned out GREAT with the extra lemon (and, of course, powdered sugar on top). I also added a dash of salt to the crust and thought it was divine. These weren't anything flashy or out of the ordinary...just exactly what lemon bars should taste like.

Fantastic! The crust was nice, crisp, and buttery- exactly how I love it. And the lemon filling was just right. I took the advice of other reviewers and added the lemon zest. 

Also a tip to make sure you get maxiumum juiciness out of your lemons- pop them in the microwave for about 15 seconds. They yield much more juice this way! 

Very lemony, easy, and satisfying! Throw away the boxed stuff and make these!

With nearly 1,000 reviews, I don't know that I'm adding much, but these are my favorite dessert to make for myself, throwing parties, and to bring to events. I make three minor adjustments based on other reviews: add 1/4 tsp salt to crust; use 2/3 cup fresh-squeezed lemon juice (more precise than measuring by number of lemons); add 1 Tbsp flour to custard because of extra juice. The result: perfection. Everyone loves them, everyone asks for my recipe, and friends give me lemons from their trees because they want lemon bars in return. I really can't say enough good things about these.

Well my crust was a bit soft on the side by my oven and that edge it kinda absorbed the filling. I used 2/3cup or so(2 med lemons but lite on juice so I added about the amount of 1 lemon of bottle juice) I think it made it a bit more tart I liked this. I also added the zest of 1 lemon to the filling. After the yummy but thin result and reading the reviews I have planned to ..still add Xtra juice from bottle, to 2/3cup,use the 11×8 pan and to chill the crust A bit to get even when pushing it out. The parchment works great and I can't wait to make again.

Such a great recipe. I took suggestions and used 2/3 cup juice, 1 extra tbs. flour to filling, zest of 2 lemons.Add 1/4 tsp salt to crust plus 1 tsp zest to crust. Used 8x11 pan and increased cooking time 5-10 min for the crust, as well as 5-10 min. with the filling . Enjoy!

These lemon bars are a crowd pleaser and soooo delicious. I'm at high altitude (6,000 ft), so I bake both the shortbread and the total at 375 degrees. You may have to adjust the cook timing. Just keep a good watch on it. I also add 1 tbsp of flour to the shortbread and 1 tbsp flour and 1 tbsp corn starch to the custard filling. Do not substitute the white sugar. My experimentation shows it works best. I add the zest of the lemons for added kick. Cheers!

I made these for an art opening reception, and got rave reviews! I did make a couple of changes, mostly additions. In the crust I added about 1/2 t. of salt and 1 tsp of vanilla. To the filling I added the zest from the 2 lemons, and about 1 tbls of lemoncello liquer and equal amount of additional flour to balance it out. I followed someone's suggestion to sift the confectioner's sugar while they are still hot, so that it sets and to cut them into squares the next day- they came out clean and pretty!

Delicious! I took the advice of others and baked the crust longer and added 2/3 c lemon juice and the zest of one lemon to the filling. I whipped it for a few minutes to make it fluffier. Served slightly warm with powdered sugar.

The Perfect Lemon Lover’s Lemon Bar! AFTER making a few changes: I added 1 tsp lemon zest to crust I added 1 tsp Vanilla Extract to crust I added 2 tsp lemon zest to filling I used 1/2 cup of lemon juice (4 sm lemons) Note: My pan was slightly larger than the recommended 9x13. Now a 5 STAR Lemon Bar!

Delicious. I doubled the filling ingredients and left the crust as is for a 9x13 pan and thought the ratio was perfect. I juiced 3 lemons which proudced 6 oz. of juice, and then added 2 oz of jarred lemon juice for a total of 8 oz. I added 2 T. extra flour to the filling and also added the zest from 2 lemons. After baking 25 mins, the top and sides had begun to brown and their was very little to no shake to the filling, so I took them out of the oven. The result was wonderful!

I used a 9x9" pan and baked the crust for 30 minutes, followed by the filling for 35 minutes. The crust turned out a little overdone (my bad, maybe would've stuck with 20 minutes instead). I used 2/3 cup of lemon juice and the zest of 2 lemons + 1tbsp of extra flour (per comments suggestion), then finished it off with a dusting of powdered sugar. I'd make again!
It's amazing but next time that I maje it, I'll add way less sugar
Love it! Would’ve used a little more lemon juice for my taste

Very good. I love lemon bars, and largely followed this recipe. The only changes I made was to add some extra lemon extract, as well as a pinch of salt to both the crust and custard. They came out beautifully and full of flavor.

I’ve made these like 7 times I add lemon zest from the 2 lemons in mix . All the folks I made them for loved them!!!!! And so did I, I wrap up mine with plastic wrap and put them in a freezer bag. They freeze well.
I'm not sure what happened but I followed the instructions and they did not turn out anything like the picture, I'm English though and I'm used to using precise measurements not these stupid cups.
Delicious
They are super easy to make. and taste amazing
The crust is a little thick and a 9x13 but once you pour your butter over the top and it soaks into that this is my second time making it and by George it's good
